nodes.name: camera_follows
nodes.summary: Declares the follow camera: remembers where the sprite sits, points the background at it, then each frame scrolls the world by the sprite's drift and puts the sprite back before it is drawn.

nodes.name: NeedsGameLoop
nodes.summary: Guardrail check: reports a `camera_follows` declared in a program whose follow routine is never called, which means no game loop is there to run it.

nodes.name: keep_showing.rb
nodes.summary: Effect pack for `keep_showing`: a picture painted when it changes and then left alone. It repaints once per page the screen keeps, so a tear-free (double-buffered) screen cannot flicker between the new value and the old.

nodes.name: KeepShowing
nodes.summary: The pack module: the `keep_showing` verb, the per-builder table of declared pictures, the Shown handle, and the guardrail for one that is never drawn.

nodes.name: keep_showing
nodes.summary: Declares a named picture, builds its drawing block into a routine of its own so it costs its code once, and hands back a Shown handle; a duplicate name or a missing block is a friendly error.

nodes.name: Shown
nodes.summary: The handle a game holds: `.changed` owes one paint per page the screen keeps, `.draw` pays one off where the picture belongs in the frame, and `.cancel` drops what is still owed so an old banner cannot follow a new game.

nodes.name: NeverDrawn
nodes.summary: Guardrail check: reports a keep_showing picture that is declared but whose routine is never called, so the picture never appears at all.

nodes.name: menu.rb
nodes.summary: Effect pack for `menu`: an ordered list of rows, a cursor moved by up/down that wraps and steps over disabled rows, a held-button repeat, a per-row block run on the press edge, and the drawing of all of it in the menu's three colours.

nodes.name: Menus
nodes.summary: The pack module: the `menu` verb plus the movement, choosing, drawing and argument-checking helpers, all written in public DSL verbs (var, held, pressed, .then, draw_text).

nodes.name: Items
nodes.summary: Collector for the `m.item` calls inside a menu block: validates each row's label (one string, or a list of words with a value deciding which), its enabled flag and its colour overrides, and gathers them into Item records.

nodes.name: Menu
nodes.summary: The handle a game keeps: which row is picked (readable and settable), a Condition true on the frame the pick changed, and the build-time row count.

nodes.name: menu
nodes.summary: The `menu` verb: validates the rows, placement, button, origin, spacing and repeat delay, allocates the pick/wait/moved variables, then wires movement, choosing and drawing into the frame and checks the glyphs still fit the sprite table.

nodes.name: menu_move
nodes.summary: Reads up and down each frame, steps the pick once and then again every repeat_every frames while a direction is held, and records that the pick moved.

nodes.name: menu_draw
nodes.summary: Draws every row each frame: the dim colour for a row that cannot be picked, and otherwise a two-colour pair keyed on the pick so one glyph sprite changes colour instead of two rows being drawn.

nodes.name: NeedsGameLoop
nodes.summary: Guardrail check: a menu reads the buttons and redraws its rows every frame, so one declared in a program with nothing pacing the frames is reported.

nodes.name: pulse.rb
nodes.summary: Effect pack for `pulse`: a tiled sprite that grows to a size, shrinks back and keeps doing it. The rhythm is a counter walked once a frame rather than a comparison against the size, so an overshoot can never leave it stuck.

nodes.name: Pulse
nodes.summary: The pack module: the `pulse` verb, the per-sprite state and per-frame routine, the seconds-to-frames conversion, and the size checks.

nodes.name: pulse
nodes.summary: Declares the rhythm for one sprite: works the half-cycle out in frames, validates the two sizes, and sets the top, the bottom and the per-frame step. Called again on the same sprite it replaces the old rhythm.

nodes.name: pulse_state
nodes.summary: Allocates this sprite's pulse variables once and installs the once-a-frame routine that walks the counter, wraps it, and eases `sprite.scale` toward whichever end of the pulse it is heading for.

nodes.name: NeedsGameLoop
nodes.summary: Guardrail check: reports a pulse whose per-frame routine is declared but never called, so the sprite never breathes.

nodes.name: screen_fade.rb
nodes.summary: Effect pack for the scene change and the hit flash: `fade_out`, `fade_in`, `flash_screen` and `fade_level`. It walks the display's fade or tint amount over frames in a variable that holds a fraction, so a fade lands on exactly the frame the author asked for.
nodes.languageNotes: Black and white are a brightness change (the display's `fade`); every other colour is mixed in (`tint`). One routine covers both by branching on a colour settled at build time, so a frame that is not fading costs nothing.

nodes.name: ScreenFade
nodes.summary: The pack module: the four fade verbs, the hidden level/target/step/colour/active variables, the per-frame ramp, the frames-or-seconds conversion, and the rules about where in the layer stack a fade may sit.

nodes.name: fade_out
nodes.summary: Starts a fade toward a colour over frames or seconds, optionally placed under a named layer so a HUD in front of it stays readable.

nodes.name: fade_in
nodes.summary: Brings the screen back from a fade; with no arguments it returns in the colour it faded to over the same number of frames, so a scene change is two words and no bookkeeping.

nodes.name: flash_screen
nodes.summary: Sets the level full and ramps it back to nothing — the impact flash, which is a fade run the other way in a hurry.

nodes.name: start_fade
nodes.summary: The shared entry all three verbs go through: checks where the fade is allowed to sit in the stack, records the colour, the target level and the per-frame step, and arms the ramp.

nodes.name: screen_fade_state
nodes.summary: Declares the hidden fade variables once and installs the once-a-frame routine that branches on the colour, calls `fade` or `tint` at the current level, and stops itself when the level reaches its target.

nodes.name: FadedOutNeverIn
nodes.summary: Guardrail check: reports a program that fades out and never brings the picture back, which leaves the game running behind a flat screen.

nodes.name: NeedsGameLoop
nodes.summary: Guardrail check: a fade is walked frame by frame, so one declared in a program with no frames to run on is reported.

nodes.name: screen_shake.rb
nodes.summary: Effect pack for `shake_screen`: four hidden variables and a once-a-frame routine that moves the camera to alternating sides for a count of frames and then puts the picture back exactly where it was. The framework's worked example of what a pack is.
nodes.languageNotes: The jitter alternates rather than being random, so the same hit shakes the same way every time and the ROM backend and the reference interpreter agree frame for frame.

nodes.name: ScreenShake
nodes.summary: The pack module: the `shake_screen` verb, the left/power/direction/offset variables, the per-frame jitter routine, and the frames-or-seconds conversion.

nodes.name: shake_screen
nodes.summary: Arms a shake: how far the picture moves and for how many frames (or seconds). Called again mid-shake it restarts rather than queueing, so repeated hits keep shaking.

nodes.name: screen_shake_state
nodes.summary: Declares the shake variables once and installs the per-frame routine that flips the side, moves the camera by power times direction, and restores the picture when the count runs out.

nodes.name: NeedsGameLoop
nodes.summary: Guardrail check: reports a `shake_screen` whose per-frame routine is never called, so the shake is armed and nothing walks it.

nodes.name: emulator.rb
nodes.summary: The single seam between ruby-gba and the emulator it verifies ROMs on. It loads the ruby-gba-emulator gem (falling back to a sibling checkout) and raises a clear, actionable error when it is absent rather than quietly skipping verification.

nodes.name: Emulator
nodes.summary: Module-function API — load!, open, probe, available? — that everything needing a real core goes through, so the backing emulator can be swapped in one place.

nodes.name: load!
nodes.summary: Requires the emulator gem first and the sibling checkout second, so a normal install builds the C extension per Ruby ABI instead of resolving a stale vendored path.

nodes.name: evaluated_game.rb
nodes.summary: A game's block, run — the one place a DSL block becomes a program. It makes a Builder, evaluates the block (catching `debug_halt`'s throw), emits the deferred function bodies and takes the op-tree, so the four steps cannot drift between callers.

nodes.name: EvaluatedGame
nodes.summary: Making one runs the block, so no caller can do three of the four steps. It also exposes what the run learned that the tree cannot hold — unbranched conditions, dropped frame syncs, software sprites, dump requests — which is what the guardrails read.

nodes.name: field_ref.rb
nodes.summary: A mutable handle to one field of one pool instance at a run-time slot index — what a pool's `each` hands you as `b.x`. It reads and writes that slot in the field's backing list, so it behaves like an ordinary variable even though it lives at a computed index.

nodes.name: FieldRef
nodes.summary: A Value subclass whose read is a list index rather than a named variable. It overrides set/add/sub/clamp/approach/abs/flip to write that slot through a scratch variable, and carries the fraction scale the field's declared default implies.

nodes.name: flicker.rb
nodes.summary: Measures, on a real run, whether a tear-free (double-buffered) program is losing half its drawing. A pixel where the two pictures disagree and neither of them changed over two frame boundaries is stuck, and the player is watching it flicker.
nodes.languageNotes: The exact complement of the tearing check: a tear-free screen keeps two pictures and can lose half a drawing, a direct-colour screen keeps one and can be caught halfway, so only one of the two questions is ever asked of a program.

nodes.name: Flicker
nodes.summary: Holds the Reading value object (how many pixels are stuck, and where the first one is, with `measured?` so 'we did not look' cannot read as 'nothing was wrong'), the screen test, and the comparison rule.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Compares both pictures at one frame boundary against both two boundaries later, counts the pixels that disagree with nothing coming to fix them, and reports the first one's coordinates once past the noise floor.

nodes.name: font.rb
nodes.summary: The bitmap font model: glyphs stored as row-bytes plus the metrics to lay them out. Each glyph carries its own width, so a proportional font advances by the glyph in front of it rather than a fixed grid.

nodes.name: Font
nodes.summary: Knows how to walk a string's set pixels, how wide a string comes out, how many pixels a glyph lights (for the draw-cost model), and how to hand its own constructor arguments back for a dumped build.

nodes.name: Definition
nodes.summary: The collector behind `font :name do glyph … end`: takes glyphs as ASCII art or as pictures of the letters, packs each row into a byte, squares up the heights, and builds the Font.

nodes.name: each_pixel
nodes.summary: Walks the lit pixels of a string, yielding each one's offset from the text origin, advancing per glyph by that glyph's own width plus the font's spacing.

nodes.name: fonts.rb
nodes.summary: The registry of named fonts — how `draw_text … font: :tiny` resolves one — and the place the two built-ins are registered: the 5x7 uppercase default and a compact 3x5 numeric font for tight HUDs.

nodes.name: Fonts
nodes.summary: register / get / names / registered? / default over a process-local hash, so the backends and the off-screen guardrail resolve a font by name instead of reaching for one hardwired font. An unknown name raises a friendly error listing the ones that exist.

nodes.name: fraction.rb
nodes.summary: The rules for numbers that carry a fraction: writing a Float anywhere in a program is how an author says a value holds halves and quarters, and the scale then travels with the value through arithmetic so it is declared once and never repeated.
nodes.languageNotes: The scale lives in the Ruby build-time handles, never in the IR — the tree that comes out is ordinary integer arithmetic, so no backend has to learn about scales and the two cannot disagree about one.

nodes.name: Fraction
nodes.summary: DEFAULT_BITS plus `scale`, `bits_of` and `literal?` — the three questions the expression DSL asks whenever it mixes operands that may be at different scales.

nodes.name: func_dumper.rb
nodes.summary: Disassembles named lowered functions out of a finished ROM and writes the listing to a stream — the machinery behind `dump_func`, showing the machine code the lowering really produced, which the target-agnostic IR cannot reveal.

nodes.name: FuncDumper
nodes.summary: Takes the assembled ROM, the function byte spans the GBA backend recorded, and injected out/err streams (so a test can drive it with a StringIO); a bare scene name resolves to its `_scene_` function.

nodes.name: disassemble
nodes.summary: Reads the function's words out of the ROM buffer and renders each one through the Inspector's instruction decoder, addressed from the entry offset.

nodes.name: game.rb
nodes.summary: A game the DSL block declares but has not built yet. `RubyGBA.game` records the title, cartridge codes and block and hands back this handle without building or writing anything, so the tool that drives the build owns the output path and how much it prints.

nodes.name: Game
nodes.summary: Carries the two things a test builds against — the op-tree the reference interpreter runs and the finished cartridge — plus the build options a dumped IR class has to reproduce, and the registry of declared games.

nodes.name: program
nodes.summary: The op-tree the block builds, evaluated once and remembered — the block is the slowest part of a build, and every consumer treats the tree as read-only, so one tree is shared.

nodes.name: build_rom
nodes.summary: Builds the finished cartridge from the evaluated game, validating it and reporting progress to the streams it is handed.

nodes.name: grid.rb
nodes.summary: A board of equal-sized cells painted one at a time: the game talks in cell coordinates and the multiply-by-cell-size and erase-to-background arithmetic lives here. Painting only the cells that changed is also what keeps a filling board from tearing.

nodes.name: Grid
nodes.summary: set_cell / clear_cell over cell coordinates (either may be a run-time value), with build-time checks that the board fits the screen, the counts are whole and positive, and the cell size is even so the fast fill is legal.

nodes.name: hardware_sprite.rb
nodes.summary: The handle for a sprite the console composites over the background on `screen :tiled` — the same surface as the software Sprite, so the same game code works on either screen. There is no draw verb: the framework draws every hardware sprite once a frame.

nodes.name: HardwareSprite
nodes.summary: Position, movement, facing poses, rotation and scale, hide/show, animation playback, and a collision box that is per-pixel by default through the Bounds and PixelBounds mixins.

nodes.name: move
nodes.summary: Steps the sprite by a direction name or a raw dx/dy pair, and turns it to face the way it moved when it has a pose for that direction.

nodes.name: blocked_by
nodes.summary: Wires the sprite's moves to a background's solid tiles, so a step into a wall simply does not happen and the sprite slides along it with no collision code of its own.

nodes.name: face
nodes.summary: Switches the sprite to a direction's pose without moving it, composing the facing with the frame a per-direction animation is on.

nodes.name: face_angle
nodes.summary: Points the sprite at an exact heading in degrees, pivoting on its own centre — real rotation through the console's sprite hardware, not the fixed-pose swap `face` does.

nodes.name: scale
nodes.summary: Reads or sets the sprite's drawn size: with no argument it hands the size back as a Value to ease, and a size of zero or less is a friendly error pointing at `hide`.

nodes.name: image.rb
nodes.summary: Brings a photo or drawing into a game as ready-to-use pixels: loads and slices image files through a swappable adapter, marks see-through pixels with the unused 16th colour bit, and hands back plain Bitmap and Sheet data that knows nothing about ROMs.

nodes.name: Image
nodes.summary: The import entry points (load, slice, load_sheet), the transparent marker and alpha threshold, the Bitmap value object, and the errors raised when the image tool is missing or a sheet does not divide evenly.

nodes.name: Sheet
nodes.summary: A picture holding a grid of equal-size cells: hands back one cell or an arbitrary region as converted pixels, applying the alpha threshold so a cut-out's edges fall to whichever side they are closer to.

nodes.name: slice
nodes.summary: Cuts a sheet into equal-size tiles, first checking that the picture divides evenly and naming both sizes in the error when it does not.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Loads one image file at the requested on-screen size, opaque or with a cut-out background kept see-through, and returns a Bitmap of console colours.

nodes.name: image_magick.rb
nodes.summary: The ImageMagick adapter: drives `magick` (or the older `convert`) to resize-and-crop a picture and hand back raw RGB or RGBA bytes, plus the picture's own size read from its header. It knows nothing about the console's colour format.

nodes.name: ImageMagick
nodes.summary: Resolves a binary from PATH on first use, shells out through Open3, and raises a friendly BackendUnavailable naming the install command when neither command is there.

nodes.name: inspector.rb
nodes.summary: Inspects and pretty-prints GBA ROM files — the header (title, codes, entry branch, fixed byte, checksum) and a disassembly of the code — so a generated ROM can be debugged without reaching for xxd.

nodes.name: Inspector
nodes.summary: Reads a ROM from a file or straight from a built ROM object, decodes the header fields and verifies the checksum, and renders the code after the entry branch as an ARM listing.

nodes.name: code_report
nodes.summary: Formats the first instructions after the entry branch as a disassembly listing, stopping at the instruction limit it is given.

nodes.name: disassemble
nodes.summary: Decodes one ARM instruction to readable text, tracking the register values it has seen so a load or store reads as the address it really touches rather than a register name.

nodes.name: instrument.rb
nodes.summary: A playable instrument built from one recorded sample: `piano.play(:E4)` sounds a note and `play(:C4, :E4, :G4)` a chord, the whole keyboard covered by reading that one recording faster or slower.

nodes.name: Instrument
nodes.summary: A thin layer over a Sample: each note becomes a pitched voice in the mixer, shifted from the sample's own recorded note, so the author writes notes and never touches voices, rates or mixer detail.

nodes.name: ir.rb
nodes.summary: The IR barrel: requires every piece of the intermediate representation — nodes, build constructors, assets, modes, stacking, verifier, guardrails, backends, printer, palette, dump — and documents why the op-tree stays target-agnostic.

nodes.name: affine.rb
nodes.summary: The numbers behind drawing an object turned, resized or both: whole-number sine and reciprocal values in 256ths, and the inverse matrix the display walks backwards through when it asks which picture pixel lands on each screen pixel.
nodes.languageNotes: No floating point anywhere — the console has none, and every backend that draws a transformed object goes through here, so the rounding is decided in one place and the two backends land on identical pixels.

nodes.name: Affine
nodes.summary: ONE_TH (what the matrix calls 1.0), the 16-bit ceiling and minimum size, and the three module functions — sine, reciprocal and matrix — that every transformed draw is built from.

nodes.name: matrix
nodes.summary: Builds the four inverse-transform numbers for an angle and a size, holding a value too large for the 16-bit field at the maximum rather than letting it wrap round to a negative.

nodes.name: assets.rb
nodes.summary: Defines the one shared description of a declared asset (an Image and a Sample), read off the node that declares it, so the GBA lowering and the reference interpreter cannot drift about a picture's size, its see-through color, or a recording's rate. Target-agnostic by design: what a backend then does with an asset stays in that backend.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Ruby's immutable `Data.define` with a block for value objects, including `with` to derive a mirrored copy without mutating.

nodes.name: Image
nodes.summary: Immutable description of a declared picture: width, height, which color index is see-through, the raw pixels, and an authored palette order when the art came from somewhere that already chose one.

nodes.name: mirrored
nodes.summary: Returns the same picture with every row read right to left. The single place a picture is reversed, so a pose a program declares as a mirror and a pose the build notices is already one compare as identical bytes.

nodes.name: backends.rb
nodes.summary: Loads the two IR backends and documents the contract between them: a backend either interprets the IR tree (Reference, the answer key) or lowers it (GBA, which compiles a ROM), and both must honor IR::Int32's reference semantics so they agree.
nodes.languageNotes: A pure `require_relative` aggregator plus an empty namespace module — the file's value is the naming rationale recorded in its comment.

nodes.name: gba.rb
nodes.summary: The GBA lowering backend's root: it wires up every lowering collaborator, runs the prepare passes that place backgrounds, tiles, sprite art and palettes in video memory, then walks the IR tree emitting ARM7TDMI machine code in two passes (labels recorded, then branch placeholders resolved). The sibling of Backends::Reference, which interprets the same tree instead of compiling it.
nodes.languageNotes: The two-pass label/fixup design exists because an ARM branch is always four bytes however far it jumps, so emitting a placeholder never shifts a later address.

nodes.name: GBA
nodes.summary: Lowers an IR program to a Game Boy Advance ROM: owns the register conventions, the prepare passes that decide video-memory layout, the interrupt setup, and the delegation surface through which every collaborator (Emit, Drawing, Mixer, Divide, ...) is reached.

nodes.name: ObjectArt
nodes.summary: Packs sprite pictures into the console's 32K of object video memory, tracking a resident block plus a per-scene block so a scene's art is uploaded when that scene takes over and the budget a game must fit is one scene's rather than the whole game's.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Builds every lowering collaborator and registers each IR node kind's handler into the Lowering's value and statement tables, so the mapping from node kind to owner sits in one readable place instead of being scattered across case statements.

nodes.name: lower
nodes.summary: The backend's entry point: runs the prepare passes, emits boot code, walks the program's statements, appends the function bodies and data region, then resolves every branch and address fixup into the finished machine code.

nodes.name: resolve_modes
nodes.summary: Works out which display modes the program uses (direct bitmap, tear-free bitmap, tiled, rotozoom) and whether scenes switch between them, which decides how much mode management the emitted code must carry.

nodes.name: emit_irq_setup
nodes.summary: Emits the boot code that installs the interrupt handler and enables the interrupt sources the program needs (the display's frame interrupt, timer interrupts, the scanline interrupt a row bend may ride).

nodes.name: emit_irq_handler
nodes.summary: Emits the shared interrupt handler: saves the registers the interrupted code relies on, dispatches on which source fired (frame, timers, scanline), runs the frame counter and mixer tick, and acknowledges the interrupt.

nodes.name: collect_definitions
nodes.summary: The first prepare pass: walks the whole IR tree gathering every declaration (variables, lists, tables, images, fonts, sounds, songs, samples, backgrounds, sprites) so later passes and the emitters can look any of them up by name.

nodes.name: prepare_backgrounds
nodes.summary: Lays out every tiled background: banks its tiles by color count, assigns each layer its own tile-numbering base and screen blocks, and encodes the maps, so tiles and maps grow toward each other in video memory without colliding.

nodes.name: bank_the_tiles
nodes.summary: Decides, per tile, whether it can be stored at half size out of a sixteen-color palette bank or must take a whole byte per pixel, by handing the tileset's pictures to PaletteBanks.

nodes.name: prepare_one_background
nodes.summary: Places one regular tiled background: appends its tiles to video memory, encodes each of its maps into screen blocks, and records the layer's hardware settings and tile-numbering base.

nodes.name: append_tiles
nodes.summary: Writes a tileset's encoded tiles into the tile region, reusing the slot of any tile whose bytes already appeared so two tiles that come out the same picture are stored once.

nodes.name: prepare_affine_background
nodes.summary: Lays out a rotate/scale background: its maps are one byte per cell rather than a half-word, and its grid must be one of the console's square affine sizes, so tiles and maps are placed under those rules instead of the regular ones.

nodes.name: prepare_objects
nodes.summary: Plans every sprite in the program: builds the shared object palette, assigns object-memory slots scene by scene, and reports a friendly error naming the fullest scene when its art will not fit the console's 32K.

nodes.name: prepare_effect_layers
nodes.summary: Works out what a fade placed at a named layer costs: which sprites must be held out of the fade with a hardware window, and whether the twin objects that takes fit in the object table.

nodes.name: build_shared_object_palette
nodes.summary: Builds the one color table every sprite draws from, honoring an authored palette where the art brought its own order and reporting a friendly error when the program's sprites need more colors than the table holds.

nodes.name: plan_one_object
nodes.summary: Works out how one sprite will be drawn before any memory is spent: how its canvas is cut into hardware pieces, which poses mirror others, and how many object slots it will cost.

nodes.name: prepare_one_object
nodes.summary: Encodes and places one sprite's poses: trims each pose to the pixels it actually draws, shares the pieces two poses have in common, records the per-pose word the frame reads, and stores a mirrored pose as a flip rather than a second copy.

nodes.name: encode_object_tiles
nodes.summary: Turns a sprite picture (optionally cropped to a box) into the console's tiled 8x8 byte order, at half a byte per pixel when the picture fits a sixteen-color bank and a whole byte otherwise.

nodes.name: address_register.rb
nodes.summary: Tracks what a base-address register is known to still hold as instructions go past, so a variable or list access can skip rebuilding a constant base it already has. A class rather than a flag because being wrong sends a load to the wrong address, so the forgetting rule has to be readable and testable on its own.
nodes.languageNotes: The forgetting rule has three parts — any instruction that might write the register, any label (a jump target knows nothing of what came before), and any call.

nodes.name: AddressRegister
nodes.summary: Remembers the value last placed in one base register (r12 for variables, r9 for a collection) and forgets it whenever an emitted instruction, a label, or a call could have disturbed it.

nodes.name: saw
nodes.summary: Called with each emitted instruction; forgets the remembered value whenever the instruction could write this register (ASM.disturbs?, which answers yes whenever it cannot tell).

nodes.name: attribution.rb
nodes.summary: Counts what each IR node actually turned into while the code is emitted — the only moment anybody knows. Instructions are attributed exclusively (a statement is charged for its own code, never its children's), jumps are counted beside them, and nodes are keyed by identity and per use because the IR tree shares node objects.
nodes.languageNotes: Keyed by `object_id`-style identity rather than value, because IR::Node compares by shape and two identical statements written in different places are not the same statement.

nodes.name: Attribution
nodes.summary: Wraps each node's lowering, measuring the emitted byte position and branch count before and after so the difference is that node's own instruction and jump count, accumulated per node identity with how many places it was lowered from.

nodes.name: Emitted
nodes.summary: What one node emitted across every place it was lowered from: total instructions, how many of them were jumps, and how many places there were, so the cost of a single use can be asked for.

nodes.name: around
nodes.summary: Runs a node's lowering between two marks and charges the node exclusively for the instructions and jumps that appeared between them, minus whatever nested lowerings already claimed.

nodes.name: audio.rb
nodes.summary: Lowers the PSG sound ops (enable, beep, noise, wave, songs) to short lists of sound-register writes, taken from the shared Sound module so the ROM and the reference interpreter play the same thing. Also owns the vblank wait, which is where a frame's other per-frame work is hung.

nodes.name: Audio
nodes.summary: Emits the register writes behind each sound verb, builds a song's unrolled per-frame note tables, and emits the vblank wait that also steps the frame counter, snapshots input, flips a buffered page and feeds a bending background.

nodes.name: emit_play_song
nodes.summary: Emits the code that starts a song and steps it: each voice's notes become a ROM table indexed by a frame counter, so playing is a table read and a register write per frame rather than a sequencer.

nodes.name: build_song_tables
nodes.summary: Flattens a song's voices into per-frame register-value tables at build time, so no note timing has to be worked out while the game runs.

nodes.name: emit_wait_vblank
nodes.summary: Emits the wait for the safe drawing window, plus everything that belongs at a frame boundary: stepping the real-frame counter, snapshotting the keys for press-edge reads, flipping the hidden page, and handing a row bend its fresh table.

nodes.name: bend_form.rb
nodes.summary: Decides, from the program alone, which of two ways a per-row background bend is lowered: a copying engine that feeds the scroll register itself for free, or a scanline interrupt when no engine is left (sampled audio holds one). Lives in one place because both the emitter and the cost estimate must charge for the same choice.
nodes.languageNotes: A `module_function` module rather than a class — it holds no state, only an answer derived from the program.

nodes.name: BendForm
nodes.summary: Answers how many bends a program has, how many copying engines are free once sampled audio has taken its share, whether the copier path can be used, and the friendly refusal text when too many layers want to bend at once.

nodes.name: copier?
nodes.summary: True when every bending layer can ride a free copying engine, which makes the per-line cost nothing at all; false sends the bend down the scanline-interrupt path instead.

nodes.name: refusal
nodes.summary: Builds the plain-language message explaining that too many layers want to bend at once, naming how many engines there are and what has taken them.

nodes.name: bios_compress.rb
nodes.summary: Packs an embedded asset at build time into one of the two formats the console's boot ROM can expand (LZ77 or run-length), keeping whichever is smaller and reporting `:none` when neither shrinks it. Purely a GBA storage concern, so the reference interpreter reads the raw asset data and never sees a packed blob.
nodes.languageNotes: Every packed blob carries the four-byte header the BIOS reads: the scheme in the low byte's high nibble, then the expanded size in three bytes.

nodes.name: BiosCompress
nodes.summary: Implements both BIOS compression schemes and their decoders (the decoders exist so the build can verify a round trip), plus the per-build packing report the profile prints.

nodes.name: Report
nodes.summary: Exact per-build packing figures — how many blobs were packed, raw and packed byte counts, and which schemes were used — measured at build time rather than estimated.

nodes.name: best
nodes.summary: Tries both schemes on a blob and returns the smaller result, or `:none` when neither actually shrinks it — so packing can only help, never make a blob bigger.

nodes.name: lz77
nodes.summary: Encodes a blob in the BIOS sliding-window format, writing a repeated run as a short back-reference instead of the bytes themselves — which suits tile art, where the same little shapes and edges recur.

nodes.name: rle
nodes.summary: Encodes a blob in the BIOS run-length format, writing a repeated byte once with a count — which suits palettes and maps with long flat stretches.

nodes.name: decode
nodes.summary: Reads a packed blob's header, dispatches to the matching decoder, and hands back the expanded bytes — the build-time mirror of what the console's BIOS does at load.

nodes.name: longest_match
nodes.summary: Finds the longest earlier run matching the bytes at a position, walking a chain of previous occurrences so the LZ77 search does not rescan the whole window each time.

nodes.name: buffered.rb
nodes.summary: Drawing for the tear-free double-buffered screen, onto the hidden page. Mirrors Drawing's direct-color fills under two rules the indexed screen forces: a pixel is one byte, and video memory cannot take a lone byte, so fills move 16-bit units of two pixels and an odd edge pixel is spliced in by hand.
nodes.languageNotes: The destination is the hidden page, whose address lives in a run-time variable that swaps on every flip — so nothing here can bake the framebuffer address into an instruction.

nodes.name: Buffered
nodes.summary: Emits every drawing op for the indexed double-buffered screen: clears, rects (fixed and computed), pixels, stretched columns, blits, text and run-time digits, reaching the clip and glyph work it shares with the direct-color screen through Framebuffer.

nodes.name: emit_clear_screen_buffered
nodes.summary: Clears the hidden page (or the current `inside` area) with one transfer, filling whole 16-bit units of two identical pixel indexes.

nodes.name: emit_buffered_rect
nodes.summary: Emits a fixed-position filled rectangle on the hidden page, choosing between direct stores for a narrow one and a transfer per row (or one transfer for full-width rows) for a wide one.

nodes.name: emit_draw_rect_at_buffered_fixed_width
nodes.summary: Emits a rectangle whose position the game works out but whose width and height are known at build time, so the per-row store sequence can be unrolled for that exact width.

nodes.name: emit_buffered_rect_clip_and_rows
nodes.summary: Clips a fully computed rectangle against the screen or the current `inside` area, then emits the row loop — so a bar that empties past zero or runs off an edge needs no test in the game's own code.

nodes.name: emit_buffered_computed_row
nodes.summary: Emits one row of a rectangle whose width is only known at run time: the odd edge pixels are spliced into their 16-bit slots singly, and the even middle is filled in whole units.

nodes.name: emit_digit_routines
nodes.summary: Emits one shared glyph-drawing routine per font and width, so a run-time digit is a call rather than the glyph loop re-emitted for every digit of every number on screen.

nodes.name: emit_pixel_buffered_runtime
nodes.summary: Writes a single pixel at a position the game works out: reads the 16-bit slot holding it, splices the color index into the correct half, and writes the slot back, since a lone byte write would corrupt its neighbor.

nodes.name: emit_draw_column_at_buffered
nodes.summary: Emits a stretched picture column — the first-person wall strip — on the hidden page: one walk down the screen fills every pixel of the strip's width, clipped top and bottom, with see-through rows skipped.

nodes.name: emit_blit_row_span
nodes.summary: Copies one row of a solid picture onto the hidden page as whole 16-bit units, which is why a buffered blit must start on an even column and be an even number of pixels wide.

nodes.name: collision.rb
nodes.summary: Lowers per-pixel sprite collision — the shape-accurate half of `overlaps?`. Builds a one-byte-per-pixel solid table for every pose at build time, then emits an inline walk of the rectangle where two sprites' boxes meet, asking whether any pixel is drawn in both at once.
nodes.languageNotes: Keeps its working state in hidden IWRAM variables rather than juggling registers, which is safe because a collision test never runs nested inside another.

nodes.name: Collision
nodes.summary: Prepares each sprite's solid-pixel masks and emits the run-time overlap walk, evaluating the test's own operands (both sprites' x, y and current pose) through the shared Lowering rather than through whichever file owns those node kinds.

nodes.name: prepare_pixel_masks
nodes.summary: Walks the program for per-pixel overlap tests and registers a solid-pixel table for each sprite they name, so only the sprites that actually collide pay for one.

nodes.name: mask_bytes
nodes.summary: Turns a pose's pixels into one byte per pixel (1 drawn, 0 see-through), laid out pose after pose so the showing frame's table is base plus pose times width times height.

nodes.name: eval_pixels_overlap
nodes.summary: Emits the whole per-pixel test as a value: stashes both sprites' positions and mask addresses, computes the overlapping rectangle, walks it, and leaves 0 or 1 in the accumulator.

nodes.name: walk_overlap
nodes.summary: Emits the nested row/column walk over the overlapping rectangle, reading one byte from each sprite's mask and leaving early with a hit the moment both are drawn.

nodes.name: divide.rb
nodes.summary: Dividing by a number the game works out, without the console's own divide routine. The chip has no divide instruction; this emits a hand-written long division whose step count is found by five scaling compares and whose steps are unrolled, so the code jumps into the ladder at the right place and no step pays for a branch.
nodes.languageNotes: Copied into IWRAM at boot with a fixed byte budget per routine, and the build fails by name if either ever outgrows its reservation.

nodes.name: Divide
nodes.summary: Decides whether a program needs the divide routines at all, reserves their IWRAM room, emits them and the boot-time copy, and emits the calls — covering both whole-number division and the wider fixed-point one.

nodes.name: needs_divide_routine?
nodes.summary: Scans the program for a division whose divisor is worked out at run time — the only kind that cannot be folded into a shift or a reciprocal multiply — so a game that never does one ships no routine.

nodes.name: emit_copy_divide_routines_to_iwram
nodes.summary: Emits the boot-time copy that moves the divide routines from the cartridge into the console's zero-wait-state internal memory, where they run about two and a third times faster.

nodes.name: emit_divide_routine
nodes.summary: Emits the whole-number divide routine: signs set aside, the divisor scaled under the numerator, a jump into the unrolled ladder, then the signs restored.

nodes.name: emit_divide_fix_routine
nodes.summary: Emits the fixed-point divide, which walks the full width of the answer so a fraction divided by a fraction keeps its fraction, and saturates rather than wrapping when the answer will not fit.

nodes.name: emit_divide_ladder
nodes.summary: Writes the 32 division steps out one after another rather than as a loop, each a compare, a conditional subtract and a doubling that slides the compare's answer into the quotient.

nodes.name: drawing.rb
nodes.summary: Direct-color (Mode 3) drawing plus the screen-mode and page management around it — screens, backgrounds, tiles, cameras, fades, tints, hardware sprites, text and digits. Ten statement kinds fork here on which screen is live, handing the tear-free ones to Buffered, while the work both framebuffer screens share lives in Framebuffer.
nodes.languageNotes: What the prepare passes decide about a program arrives as one `layout` record set after construction, because none of it exists when this object is built.

nodes.name: Drawing
nodes.summary: The largest lowering collaborator: emits every drawing statement for the direct-color screen, enters and leaves each display mode, uploads a scene's art, writes the object table each frame, and owns the fade and blend arithmetic a tint and a see-through layer share.

nodes.name: emit_screen
nodes.summary: Lowers a `screen` declaration: picks the console's display mode, sets the display-control register, and marks which mode the rest of the lowering should assume from here.

nodes.name: emit_boot_screen
nodes.summary: Emits the boot-time display setup for whichever screen the program declared, before any of the game's own drawing runs.

nodes.name: enter_buffered_mode
nodes.summary: Switches the display to the tear-free indexed bitmap mode and initializes the back-buffer address variable that every buffered draw writes through.

nodes.name: emit_scene_art_upload
nodes.summary: Emits the copy that sends a scene's own sprite pictures into video memory when that scene takes over, which is what lets a game hold more art than one scene's 32K budget.

nodes.name: emit_pixel
nodes.summary: Writes one direct-color pixel, taking a fully constant position to a single store and a computed one to a bounds check plus an address computed from the row stride.

nodes.name: emit_dma_fill_rect
nodes.summary: Fills a rectangle through the console's copying engine, using one transfer when the rows are full width and one per row otherwise.

nodes.name: emit_draw_column_at
nodes.summary: Emits the stretched picture column a first-person view is made of: one walk down the screen fills the whole strip, the source row found by multiplying rather than dividing, clipped at both ends.

nodes.name: emit_draw_rect_at_computed
nodes.summary: Emits a rectangle whose position and size the game all works out, clipping it against the screen or the current `inside` area so a bar that empties past zero draws nothing rather than wrapping.

nodes.name: emit_set_tile
nodes.summary: Changes one cell of a tiled background while the game runs — a door opening, a block broken — as a single half-word write, silently doing nothing when the cell is off the map.

nodes.name: emit_show_map
nodes.summary: Swaps the whole background to another of its declared maps, copying it in at the frame boundary and only on a frame where the answer actually changed — so `show_map` can be written every frame.

nodes.name: emit_affine_background
nodes.summary: Emits a rotate/scale background's per-frame work: the 2x2 transform matrix from its angle and size, and the reference point that keeps the pivot at the middle of the screen.

nodes.name: emit_fade
nodes.summary: Sets the display's brightness blend so the whole screen moves toward black or white without anything being redrawn, and hands the blend back to a see-through layer when the fade lifts.

nodes.name: emit_present_object
nodes.summary: Writes one sprite's entries into the console's object table each frame, dispatching between the plain upright draw, the per-pose-word draw a trimmed or mirrored cycle needs, and the transformed draw a turning or resizing sprite needs.

nodes.name: emit_rect_row_dma
nodes.summary: The shared row-by-row transfer behind fills, blits and backing saves: sets the source, destination and control words and clips each row against the screen or the current area.

nodes.name: emit_blit_transparent
nodes.summary: Copies a cut-out picture pixel by pixel, skipping the see-through ones, with each row clipped against the screen edges in the high registers.

nodes.name: emit_digit_routines
nodes.summary: Emits one shared glyph routine per font and digit width for the direct-color screen, so a run-time number costs a call per digit rather than the whole glyph loop re-emitted at each one.

nodes.name: emit.rb
nodes.summary: The low-level byte emitter and the two-pass label/branch fixup machinery — the collaborator nearly every other lowering concern depends on. Fixup kinds it does not own are resolved by resolvers handed in, so Placement can add its own without this class knowing their names.
nodes.languageNotes: Also counts branches, because a jump is made here and Attribution needs to know whether a node's code runs the way it is written.

nodes.name: Emit
nodes.summary: Holds the growing code buffer, the label table, the pending fixups, the data blobs, and the two address registers whose remembered contents let a variable or list access skip rebuilding its base.

nodes.name: emit_branch
nodes.summary: Writes a four-byte placeholder that remembers which label it wants and forgets both address registers, since a jump target knows nothing of what a register held on the way here.

nodes.name: resolve_fixups
nodes.summary: The second pass: now that every label's position is known, rewrites each placeholder — branches and data or label addresses directly, and any other kind through the resolver its owner supplied.

nodes.name: resolve_branch
nodes.summary: Turns one branch placeholder into a real ARM branch by computing the signed word offset from the instruction to its label, honoring the pipeline's two-instruction lead.

nodes.name: expressions.rb
nodes.summary: Evaluates every value node — arithmetic, comparisons, bit operations, fixed-point multiply and divide, table reads, and the button reads — leaving each answer in the accumulator register. This is where a divisor written in the program becomes a shift or a reciprocal multiply and only a computed one reaches the divide routine.

nodes.name: Expressions
nodes.summary: Emits the code behind each value kind, folding constant divisors and moduli into shifts, masks or reciprocal multiplies at build time and falling back to the emitted divide routine only when the divisor is worked out as the game runs.

nodes.name: eval_table_get
nodes.summary: Reads one element of a build-time ROM table, making an out-of-range index safe by masking when the length is a power of two and clamping against both ends otherwise.

nodes.name: eval_binop
nodes.summary: The main arithmetic dispatch: folds the constant-operand cases first, otherwise evaluates both sides and emits the add, multiply, shift, bit operation, division or comparison.

nodes.name: emit_constant_binop
nodes.summary: Recognizes an operation with a number written in the program on one side and emits the cheap form for it — a shift for a power of two, a mask for a modulo, a reciprocal multiply for any other fixed divisor.

nodes.name: emit_reciprocal_divide
nodes.summary: Divides by a fixed non-power-of-two by multiplying with a build-time reciprocal and keeping the high half of the 64-bit product, then correcting the sign.

nodes.name: eval_mul_fix
nodes.summary: Multiplies two fixed-point numbers at full 64-bit width and shifts the scale back out, so the author never has to spot which of their multiplies would have overflowed.

nodes.name: eval_pressed
nodes.summary: Reads a button on its press edge by comparing this frame's key snapshot against last frame's, which is why the vblank code snapshots the keys once per frame.

nodes.name: framebuffer.rb
nodes.summary: What the direct-color and tear-free screens share: where drawing may land right now (an `inside` area or the whole screen), a fill's control words, walking a stretched picture column, and the run-time digit glyph loop. Neither screen owns this; it is the shape a framebuffer has whichever one is live.
nodes.languageNotes: A picture row becomes a screen row by dividing by the picture's height — a shift for a power-of-two height, and for any other a build-time reciprocal multiply that costs one instruction more.

nodes.name: Framebuffer
nodes.summary: Holds the clip bounds both bitmap screens honor, the transfer control words, the stretched-column setup including its per-column run tables, and the shared digit glyph loop.

nodes.name: ColumnDivide
nodes.summary: How a stretched column turns a screen row into a picture row without a divide: a shift for a power-of-two picture height, a build-time reciprocal otherwise, plus the spare rows the rounding-down needs at the far end.

nodes.name: emit_column_setup
nodes.summary: Sets up a stretched column draw: resolves the source picture and slice, works out the row step, and bails early when the requested height is zero or less.

nodes.name: emit_column_runs
nodes.summary: Uses the build-time table of where each picture column actually holds pixels, so a mostly see-through picture costs the rows that draw rather than its full height.

nodes.name: emit_clip_column_rows
nodes.summary: Clips a stretched column's top and bottom against the screen or the current `inside` area, advancing the source position by however many rows were cut so a wall you stand against needs no test around it.

nodes.name: emit_digit_glyph_loop
nodes.summary: The body of the shared run-time digit routine: walks a glyph's cells out of a build-time table and plots the lit ones, holding the cell's x, y and color in the high registers across the whole walk.

nodes.name: frames.rb
nodes.summary: How many frames a pass of the game loop really took. The display raises its own interrupt sixty times a second whatever the game is doing, so counting there makes the answer exact and free, and the difference between one pass and the next is how many frames the last pass spanned.
nodes.languageNotes: Holds no state of its own — the count and its marks live in named variables shared with the IR, so this is two emission recipes rather than a real collaborator.

nodes.name: Frames
nodes.summary: Emits the interrupt-side frame counter and the per-pass step that turns the difference between two counts into how many real frames the last pass spanned, capped so a very late pass is never asked to catch up.

nodes.name: emit_frame_step
nodes.summary: Computes how many display frames passed since the last time the game loop came round, clamps it to the cap, and leaves it where the per-frame routines read it.

nodes.name: functions.rb
nodes.summary: Emits the bodies of a program's routines after the main code, behind a leading endless loop so the main flow cannot run off its end into the first body. Only the routines that stay in the cartridge are emitted here; the ones chosen to run from the console's quick memory are emitted as one copied block by Placement.

nodes.name: Functions
nodes.summary: Emits one function body per declared routine (saving the return address and restoring it as the program counter), emits the `case` dispatch that runs exactly one scene per frame, and switches display modes on a scene change when the program mixes them.

nodes.name: emit_one_function
nodes.summary: Emits a single routine — the shared shape for a cartridge-resident one and one copied into quick memory — including a scene's preamble and art upload when the routine is a scene.

nodes.name: emit_case
nodes.summary: Emits the scene dispatch: reloads the state variable before each comparison, because a scene call clobbers the accumulator register the comparison would otherwise reuse.

nodes.name: layer_blend.rb
nodes.summary: Seeing through one layer to what is behind it. The console blends as it draws the scanline, so nothing is redrawn and a see-through layer costs the same whatever is on screen. Two paths — a scenery layer named in the blend-control register, or a sprite layer marked one bit at a time in its own table entry — and the author never learns which they got.
nodes.languageNotes: Neither path survives a fade: a see-through sprite still has to be told what it blends with, and a fade writes that register whole — measured, keeping the far side across a fade leaves half-bright ghosts on a black screen.

nodes.name: LayerBlend
nodes.summary: Owns which layer a program can be seen through and by how much: reads the stacking picture once it exists, emits the boot-time blend setup, and re-emits the blend when a fade that borrowed it lifts.

nodes.name: prepare_layer_blend
nodes.summary: Finds the program's one see-through layer and its starting amount, which may be a number written in the program or something the game works out each frame.

nodes.name: emit_see_through
nodes.summary: Emits the register write for a blend amount the game works out, placed at the frame boundary so fog that thickens costs one write per frame and nothing per pixel.

nodes.name: emit_blend_amount
nodes.summary: Turns a 0-to-100 transparency into the console's pair of sixteenths weights for the near and far sides of the blend, and writes them.

nodes.name: far_side_bits
nodes.summary: Works out which hardware layers sit behind the see-through one and must therefore be named as the far side of the blend, including the backdrop.

nodes.name: lists.rb
nodes.summary: Allocates and emits the runtime collections. A list that is shifted becomes a ring (a power-of-two block so the wrap is one bitwise AND); a list that is only indexed stays a plain array, where the physical slot is the index and no rounding is paid for. Either way a bad index stays inside the list, mirroring what the reference interpreter allows.
nodes.languageNotes: A sprite's save-under backing buffer shares this file because it shares the IWRAM allocation story — a name registered once, a layout looked up afterward — not because it is a list.

nodes.name: Lists
nodes.summary: Registers each list with its capacity, element width and storage shape, places it in quick or roomy memory, and emits push, drop, set, get and length against whichever shape it got.

nodes.name: register_list
nodes.summary: Records a list's capacity, element width and whether it is shifted, rounding a ring up to the next power of two and allocating its hidden length (and head) variables.

nodes.name: place_list
nodes.summary: Puts a list in the console's quick memory when a frame touches it and in the roomier, slower memory otherwise, honoring an explicit `fast:` either way.

nodes.name: register_backing
nodes.summary: Reserves the save-under buffer a software sprite needs to restore what it covered, allocated through the same name-then-look-up path a list uses.

nodes.name: emit_list_push
nodes.summary: Appends an item: computes the destination slot from head and length for a ring or straight from length for a plain array, stores the element at its width, and grows the length unless the list is full.

nodes.name: emit_list_drop
nodes.summary: Removes from the front or the back: dropping from the front moves the ring's head rather than shifting any element, which is the whole reason a shifted list is stored as a ring.

nodes.name: emit_slot_address
nodes.summary: Turns a logical index into a real address, masking against the ring's power-of-two block or bounding against the plain array's length, and reusing the base held in the collection's address register when it is still there.

nodes.name: emit_bound_to_capacity
nodes.summary: Keeps an index inside a plain array by comparing against its own length and reading slot zero instead, so a bad index can pick up a stale slot but can never reach a neighbouring variable.

nodes.name: loop_form.rb
nodes.summary: Decides which shape a `repeat` is lowered to, from the loop's body alone: counter and limit kept in registers (four instructions a pass) where nothing in the body can disturb them, or in memory (sixteen) where it can. Lives in one place because the emitter and the cost estimate must charge for the same shape.
nodes.languageNotes: The blockers are named explicitly — statement kinds that reach code the loop does not control, and the lowerings that use the high registers for their own working.

nodes.name: LoopForm
nodes.summary: Answers whether a loop can keep its counter in registers, how few statements are worth bracketing around a blocker before giving the registers up, and the plain-language phrase naming what blocked it.

nodes.name: registers?
nodes.summary: The decision itself: true when nothing in the loop's body can touch the two high registers the fast shape keeps its counter and limit in.

nodes.name: spills?
nodes.summary: True when the body's blockers are few enough to bracket — saving and restoring the pair around each — which still pays at two and does not at three.

nodes.name: reason
nodes.summary: Names what kept a loop off the fast shape, so the profile can explain a loop's cost rather than just report it.

nodes.name: phrase_for
nodes.summary: Turns a blocking statement or value kind into plain language — a routine call, a nested loop, a run-time divide, raw instructions — for the profile's explanation.

nodes.name: lowering.rb
nodes.summary: Dispatches a node by its kind through two plain kind-keyed Hashes (values and statements) rather than a case statement, so a kind's handler is data registered once in GBA#initialize. That indirection is what lets two collaborators each need the other's node kind without depending on each other.
nodes.languageNotes: Two tables rather than one because a value handler and a statement handler are different contracts: a value leaves its answer in the accumulator, a statement leaves nothing live.

nodes.name: Lowering
nodes.summary: Holds the value and statement handler tables, routes every node through Attribution so each one's emitted instructions are counted, tracks the live display mode and the current `inside` clip area, and raises a clear error on an unknown kind.

nodes.name: value
nodes.summary: Lowers one value node through its registered handler, wrapped in Attribution so the instructions it emits are charged to that node. Every value node in the program passes through here.

nodes.name: statement
nodes.summary: Lowers one statement node through its registered handler, likewise attributed. Every statement in the program passes through here, which is why the counting lives in this class.

nodes.name: in_mode
nodes.summary: Runs a block with a given display mode in force and restores the previous one after, which is how a scene that declares its own screen gets its drawing lowered for that screen.

nodes.name: inside
nodes.summary: Runs a block with a clip area in force so everything lowered inside it is cut off at that rectangle's edges rather than drawn and covered up; areas do not nest.

nodes.name: memory.rb
nodes.summary: The IWRAM allocator, which hands memory out from both ends. A variable is reached by a twelve-bit distance from the base, so variables grow up from the base where being near it is worth two instructions instead of four, and everything else grows down from the ceiling. Also owns the separate 256K of roomier, slower memory.
nodes.languageNotes: There is no freeing, because nothing in a running program ever gives its memory back; everything is rounded up to a whole word so both ends stay aligned.

nodes.name: Memory
nodes.summary: A two-ended bump allocator over the console's 32K of quick memory plus a one-ended one over its 256K of roomier memory, reporting how much of each is used, free, or overrun.

nodes.name: alloc_near_base
nodes.summary: Allocates growing up from the base, which is where variables go so their distance fits the load instruction's twelve bits and each read costs two instructions rather than four.

nodes.name: alloc
nodes.summary: Allocates growing down from the ceiling — lists, mixer buffers, row-bend tables, and the block of code moved into quick memory — leaving the gap between the two ends as what is free.

nodes.name: alloc_roomy
nodes.summary: Allocates from the console's separate 256K chip — eight times the room and about six times the wait on a read — which is where a collection no frame touches goes.

nodes.name: mixer.rb
nodes.summary: The software mixer for sampled audio. The console's sampled-audio hardware plays one stream of bytes, so the CPU sums every sounding voice into a buffer each frame while the copying engine plays the other of two buffers out. Owns registering samples as ROM data as well as the mix that uses them.
nodes.languageNotes: The mix routine is copied into IWRAM at boot under a snug byte budget, because every byte reserved here is a byte the routines a frame spends its time in do not get.

nodes.name: Mixer
nodes.summary: Prepares the sampled-audio hardware (timer, FIFO, copying engines, double buffers), allocates the fixed voice slots, emits play and stop, and emits the per-frame mix routine that sums every sounding voice at its own pitch step.

nodes.name: prepare_direct_sound
nodes.summary: Registers every declared sample as ROM data and works out the one output rate the mixer will run at, so a program with no samples pays for none of this.

nodes.name: emit_copy_mix_routine_to_iwram
nodes.summary: Copies the mix routine into zero-wait-state internal memory at boot, because its inner loop runs once per output sample per voice — thousands of times a frame — and would stall on every instruction fetch from the cartridge.

nodes.name: emit_mixer_boot
nodes.summary: Emits the boot setup for sampled audio: clears the voice slots and output buffers, configures the sound registers and FIFO, and starts the timer that clocks the output rate.

nodes.name: emit_play_sample
nodes.summary: Fills a free voice slot with a sample's ROM address, length, loop flag, level and pitch step, dropping the play quietly rather than stealing a voice when every slot is sounding.

nodes.name: emit_stop_sample
nodes.summary: Clears the voice slots belonging to one sample (or every slot when no sample is named), so a looping clip can be cut off.

nodes.name: emit_mixer_tick
nodes.summary: Runs once per displayed frame from the screen's own interrupt: swaps the two output buffers, re-arms the sound transfer, and calls the mix routine to fill the buffer the hardware is not reading.

nodes.name: emit_mix_routine
nodes.summary: The mixer's hot inner code: for each sounding voice, walks the sample at its fixed-point pitch step, scales by its level, sums into the output buffer, and retires or loops the voice when it runs out.

nodes.name: palette_banks.rb
nodes.summary: Sixteen colours to a picture, and the picture stored half the size. Counts each picture's colours and stores one using fifteen or fewer at half a byte per pixel out of a sixteen-entry bank, and anything richer at a whole byte out of the shared table. Nobody writes any of it: the author writes colour names and the count decides the rest.
nodes.languageNotes: Slot 0 of a bank is never drawn — the console reads 0 in a narrow picture as see-through in every bank — which is also exactly how art exported from anywhere else on this console is laid out.

nodes.name: PaletteBanks
nodes.summary: Does the palette arithmetic once for a set of pictures: packs the wide pictures' colours from slot 1 up, hands out whole banks of sixteen above them, shares a bank between narrow pictures that use the same colours, and reports how many came out each way.

nodes.name: allocate
nodes.summary: Runs the whole allocation: splits the pictures into wide and narrow, places the wide ones first because both kinds share one table, then hands banks to the narrow ones.

nodes.name: try_allocation
nodes.summary: Attempts one split of wide against narrow pictures, backing off a picture into the wide set when the banks run out, so a game whose pictures are all narrow gets all sixteen banks.

nodes.name: place_wide
nodes.summary: Packs every colour the wide pictures use into the shared table from slot 1 upward, so the banks can start at the first whole group of sixteen above them.

nodes.name: bank_for
nodes.summary: Finds a bank that already holds a picture's colours (or has room for them) so every frame of one walk cycle and every tile of one wall share a bank for nothing.

nodes.name: place_narrow
nodes.summary: Assigns one narrow picture its bank and records which slot each of its colours took, honoring an authored palette order where the art brought one.

nodes.name: write_banks
nodes.summary: Writes the finished colour table out — the wide colours packed low, then each bank's fifteen colours behind its never-drawn slot 0 — ready to be uploaded to the console's palette memory.

nodes.name: palette_tint.rb
nodes.summary: Tints the two screens whose pixels are indexes into a shared colour table, where the display's own mixing unit cannot help — putting the tint in the backdrop entry would turn every unpainted pixel that colour at full strength. So these screens move every entry of the table toward the colour instead, leaving the drawn picture untouched so it comes back exactly as drawn.
nodes.languageNotes: The cost is one blend per colour the game declared, never per pixel — and only on a frame where the amount or colour actually changed, so a steady tint and the common no-tint-at-all cost one compare.

nodes.name: PaletteTint
nodes.summary: Emits the tint for palette-indexed screens: a packed state word holding the colour and how far, a compare that skips the work when it has not moved, and the blend that rewrites the whole colour table when it has.

nodes.name: prepare_palette_tint
nodes.summary: Decides whether this program tints a palette-indexed screen at all, so a game that never tints ships none of the table-rewriting code.

nodes.name: emit_palette_tint
nodes.summary: The tint statement, built around a compare against the last state written: a tint that has not moved costs one comparison and a branch, and only a real change rewrites the table.

nodes.name: emit_tint_state
nodes.summary: Packs the requested colour and strength into one word, compares it against the state already in force, and branches past the whole rewrite when they match — zero steps meaning the table holds the originals whatever colour was asked for.

nodes.name: emit_tint_shares
nodes.summary: Blends one colour toward the tint using two multiplies: red and blue sit five bits apart so masking green away leaves two fields that cannot overflow into each other, and green is done on its own.

nodes.name: emit_tint_table
nodes.summary: Walks a colour table, blending every entry toward the tint and writing it into palette memory — the loop whose length is how many colours the game declared, never what is on screen.

nodes.name: emit_lift_palette_tint
nodes.summary: Puts the original colours back by re-uploading the untinted table kept in the cartridge, which is why a tint changes no drawn pixel and lifting it restores the picture exactly.

nodes.name: placement.rb
nodes.summary: Decides which lowered routines are copied into the console's 32K of fast on-die memory (IWRAM) at boot and which stay in the slow cartridge, ranking candidates by how much frame time the cost model says each one costs. Also emits the boot-time copy, the call thunks that jump to a relocated routine, and the friendly errors when insisted-on routines do not fit.
nodes.languageNotes: A whole-program placement pass: walks the IR to find the frame path, ranks routines with RoutineProfile, then rewrites call sites to branch at the relocated address.

nodes.name: Placement
nodes.summary: Mixin on the GBA backend holding the whole fast-memory placement policy: choosing routines, emitting the boot copy, resolving relocated addresses, and reporting what fit and what was passed over.

nodes.name: choose_fast_funcs
nodes.summary: Runs the two placement rounds — routines the author insisted on first, then the rest ranked by measured frame cost — and settles the final set of routines that will run from fast memory.

nodes.name: emit_copy_hot_code_to_iwram
nodes.summary: Emits the boot-time block copy that moves the chosen routines out of the cartridge into fast memory before the game starts running.

nodes.name: emit_call_func
nodes.summary: Emits a call to a routine, branching straight to it when it stayed in the cartridge and loading its relocated fast-memory address when it moved.

nodes.name: guard_fast_code_fits
nodes.summary: Checks the chosen routines still fit the memory left after variables, lists and the stack were allocated, and raises a plain-language error naming the overrun when they do not.

nodes.name: place_by_frame_cost
nodes.summary: Walks the routines in descending frame-cost order, taking each one that still fits the remaining fast memory and recording the ones passed over with what they wanted and what was left.

nodes.name: ranked_by_frame_cost
nodes.summary: Orders the placeable routines by how much of a frame the routine profile says each one spends, dropping the ones not worth moving.

nodes.name: calls_outward_from
nodes.summary: Walks the call graph outward from a starting routine to find everything reachable from it, so the frame path can be identified as a whole rather than one routine at a time.

nodes.name: guard_insisted_fits!
nodes.summary: Raises a friendly error when the routines the author explicitly marked fast: true cannot all fit, naming them and the room available.

nodes.name: primitives.rb
nodes.summary: The shared low-level helpers every other GBA lowering file spends: variable address allocation, base-plus-offset loads and stores, constant folding, and small emit helpers for adding or masking a constant.
nodes.languageNotes: Keeps the variable-memory base in a register across accesses so reading a variable is usually one instruction instead of building a full 32-bit address.

nodes.name: Primitives
nodes.summary: Holds the variable address table and the register-caching state behind the load/store helpers the rest of the lowering calls.

nodes.name: load_var
nodes.summary: Loads a variable into a register, reusing the base register when it is still live so the common case costs a single instruction.

nodes.name: store_var
nodes.summary: Stores a register back into a variable's slot, through the same shared base register the loads use.

nodes.name: emit_base
nodes.summary: Puts an address base into a register, tracking what each scratch register already holds so a repeat of the same base emits nothing.

nodes.name: emit_add_const
nodes.summary: Adds a fixed number to a register, choosing an immediate add, an immediate subtract, or a materialized constant depending on what the instruction encoding can hold.

nodes.name: emit_row_loop
nodes.summary: Emits the shared count-down loop skeleton the row-wise drawing helpers wrap their body in.

nodes.name: raster.rb
nodes.summary: Lowers the `scroll_rows` op that bends a background line by line: builds a 160-entry offset table in the gap between frames, then feeds it to the display either through a DMA copier or through a per-scanline interrupt handler.
nodes.languageNotes: The display re-reads each background's scroll position on every one of the 160 visible lines, so writing a different offset per line bends the picture without redrawing anything.

nodes.name: Raster
nodes.summary: Registers the program's row-bend declarations, allocates their offset tables, picks a DMA engine per bent layer, and emits both the table-filling loop and the scanline handler.

nodes.name: prepare_row_bends
nodes.summary: Allocates one offset table per bent background and assigns each to a DMA copier engine, falling back to the interrupt route when the engines run out.

nodes.name: emit_boot_row_bends
nodes.summary: Emits the one-time boot setup that zeroes each offset table and points its copier engine at the right background's scroll register.

nodes.name: emit_fill_row_bend_table
nodes.summary: Emits the loop that runs the author's per-row expression 160 times and writes each result into the offset table, which is the whole run-time cost of a bend.

nodes.name: emit_row_bend_handler
nodes.summary: Emits the per-scanline interrupt handler that reads the current row's offset out of the table and writes it to the background's scroll register, used when no DMA engine is free.

nodes.name: reciprocal.rb
nodes.summary: Turns division by a build-time constant into a multiply-and-shift, searching for a magic multiplier that is exactly right for all four billion numerators rather than merely most of them.
nodes.languageNotes: Granlund and Montgomery's magic-number division in the form Hacker's Delight gives it — the ARM7 has no divide instruction, so a BIOS divide costs roughly a hundred ordinary instructions.

nodes.name: Reciprocal
nodes.summary: Module-function entry point that hands back the multiplier, shift and correction a constant divisor needs to be lowered as a multiply.

nodes.name: for
nodes.summary: Public entry point: returns the recipe (multiplier, shift and whether a correction step is needed) for dividing by a given constant.

nodes.name: search
nodes.summary: Walks the shift amount upward and stops at the first one where the rounded reciprocal's error can no longer reach a whole-number boundary, so the multiply is exact for every numerator.

nodes.name: roomy.rb
nodes.summary: Decides which lists and pools get pushed out of the console's quick 32K work memory into the roomier but six-times-slower 256K, moving the coldest collections first rather than the biggest.
nodes.languageNotes: The quick memory is shared with the hot code, so a big cold collection left there silently pushes a hot routine back into the cartridge.

nodes.name: Roomy
nodes.summary: Ranks collection candidates by whether the per-frame path touches them, then moves the coldest ones until what is left fits the quick memory.

nodes.name: choose
nodes.summary: Walks the candidates coldest-first, skipping any the author explicitly pinned, and returns the set that moves to the roomy memory.

nodes.name: touched_every_frame
nodes.summary: Reads the program to find the collections named anywhere on the per-frame path — the game loop, the scenes it runs, and the routines those reach.

nodes.name: gather
nodes.summary: Collects every collection name reachable from a set of root nodes, following calls and case clauses through the IR tree.

nodes.name: save.rb
nodes.summary: Lowers the persistence ops to the cartridge's battery-backed SRAM: a marker word that tells a fresh cartridge from a saved one, then each persisted variable as four little-endian byte stores, plus the signature string emulators look for.
nodes.languageNotes: Save memory sits on an 8-bit bus, so every 4-byte value becomes four LDRB/STRB — a word-wide load would read garbage.

nodes.name: Save
nodes.summary: Stateless lowering helper for the save ops; works a slot's address out fresh each time and reaches load_var/store_var through the injected primitives.

nodes.name: emit_save_init
nodes.summary: Emits the boot check that reads the marker word out of save memory and either restores every persisted variable from its slot or leaves them at their declared defaults.

nodes.name: emit_save_store
nodes.summary: Emits the write-back of one persisted variable into its save slot, so every change to a save_var is kept without a separate save step.

nodes.name: emit_store_word_to_sram
nodes.summary: Writes a 32-bit value into save memory as four single-byte stores, shifting the value down eight bits at a time to suit the 8-bit bus.

nodes.name: statements.rb
nodes.summary: Lowers the statement-level IR ops to ARM: variable assignment and arithmetic, clamping, conditionals, and the three shapes a counted loop can take depending on which registers its body leaves free.
nodes.languageNotes: A loop's counter lives in registers where it can, is spilled around the few statements that need those registers where it must, and falls back to memory otherwise — each shape costing a different amount per pass.

nodes.name: LoopShape
nodes.summary: Immutable record of which of the three shapes a loop got (registers, spilled, or memory), how many statements a spilled loop brackets, and what in the body forced the slower shape — carried on the build record so a finished ROM can still say.
nodes.languageNotes: Data.define rather than Struct, and whether the count is in registers is derived rather than stored so the two answers cannot drift apart.

nodes.name: Statements
nodes.summary: The statement lowering pass, taking the emitter, primitives, lowering, placement and functions collaborators and turning each statement node into instructions.

nodes.name: clamp_acc_to
nodes.summary: Clamps the accumulator against one bound, folding the bound to an immediate compare when it is a build-time number and evaluating it into a register when the game works it out.

nodes.name: emit_if
nodes.summary: Lowers a conditional by evaluating the test and branching over the then-block on the inverse condition, with an extra skip branch when there is an else.

nodes.name: emit_loop
nodes.summary: Lowers the endless game loop, calling the frame routine through placement when that routine was moved to fast memory and emitting the body inline when it was not.

nodes.name: emit_repeat
nodes.summary: Entry point for a counted loop: picks the register, spilled or memory shape and dispatches to the matching emitter.

nodes.name: emit_shape
nodes.summary: Records which shape a loop got and why, so the build record and the profile report can explain a slow loop afterwards.

nodes.name: emit_repeat_in_memory
nodes.summary: The fallback loop shape: keeps the counter and limit in variable memory and reloads them each pass, used when the body needs the registers for calls, nested loops or raw instructions.

nodes.name: emit_repeat_spilled
nodes.summary: Keeps the loop counter in registers and saves the pair only around the few statements that would land in them, rather than falling all the way back to memory.

nodes.name: emit_repeat_loop
nodes.summary: Emits the shared body of a register-held counted loop — the compare, the early-exit test, the body and the branch back — for both the plain and the spilled shapes.

nodes.name: tile_vram.rb
nodes.summary: The single allocator for tiled-background video memory: hands out tile pictures packed from the bottom and map blocks from the top of the same 64K, and stops the build with an explanation when the two would meet.
nodes.languageNotes: Overlapping tiles and maps does not fail on the hardware — each writes over the other and the screen shows confetti — which is why one allocator owns both ends.

nodes.name: TileVram
nodes.summary: Tracks where tiles and maps have reached from their two ends of video memory and answers a tile's number relative to whichever base its layer counts from.

nodes.name: Full
nodes.summary: The friendly error raised when the tiles and the maps have grown into each other, naming how much each side took.

nodes.name: take_tile
nodes.summary: Reserves room for one tile picture from the bottom of video memory and hands back where it landed.

nodes.name: take_map
nodes.summary: Reserves map blocks from the top of video memory in the 2K units the hardware counts them in.

nodes.name: tile_number
